scores.evidence: push to the bot fork so upstream CI runs on a fork PR **without secrets**
scores.rationale: Technical claims are accurate including the subtle ones (10s webhook limit, fork-PR secret behavior, SKIP LOCKED queueing, HMAC verification); only trivial imprecision like lumping Modal with Firecracker.

scores.evidence: triages them (labels, priority, duplicates, requests for missing info) and, for eligible issues, writes a fix in a sandbox and opens a draft PR
scores.rationale: Covers both triage and resolution precisely, resolves ambiguities (autonomy, tenancy, trust) sensibly, and the Deferred table makes exclusions explicit with pull-forward triggers.

scores.evidence: the single module allowed to call GitHub write APIs. It checks the kill switch, policy, idempotency, and audit.
scores.rationale: One consistent design: a single write executor, a job state machine, idempotency and kill-switch decisions honored uniformly across every phase with no contradictions found.

scores.evidence: a red-team corpus of 50 injection issues causes 0 off-policy actions
scores.rationale: Each phase has checkable exit criteria tied to the plan's own named risks (injection corpus, sandbox escape tests, offline evals before enabling actions, shadow mode, eval-gated prompt changes) and validation continues online.

scores.evidence: The schema carries `installation_id` from day zero, so this is a cheap flip.
scores.rationale: Assumptions (single org, ZDR provider, own repos) are explicit, and every key decision carries a 'revisit trigger' stating what would change the design and when.

scores.evidence: A fork bomb or OOM kills the VM without touching the worker.
scores.rationale: Covers injection, memory poisoning, secret leakage, duplicates, partial failures with checkpoints, provider outages, runaway loops and sandbox escape with concrete detection and containment; only agent/human mid-work collisions are thin.

scores.evidence: staged rollout with automatic kill on SLO breach
scores.rationale: Observability, dashboards, alerting, kill switch and Terraform exist from day zero, with pinned releases, runbooks, on-call and SLOs sized to a small team before wide rollout.

scores.evidence: Org cap: $200/day. When it trips, the agent stops starting new resolves and keeps triaging.
scores.rationale: The dominant driver (inference) has per-task and org budgets, tracking of cost per merged PR, and routing to cheaper models, but engineering/build cost and overall run-cost estimates are not reasoned about.

scores.evidence: Hosted API behind a provider-agnostic interface, under a zero-data-retention (ZDR) agreement.
scores.rationale: Hard-to-reverse choices (vendor coupling, tenancy key, persisted audit/schema, single write-executor abstraction point) are isolated with explicit exit paths, while reversible choices are made quickly with revisit triggers.

scores.evidence: A **single-agent tool loop** (not multi-agent) inside a deterministic outer state machine
scores.rationale: Modular monolith, Postgres queue first, single-agent loop, and an explicit Deferred table keep the design minimal; the one forced split (sandbox) is justified as a trust boundary.

scores.evidence: replaying one webhook delivery 10× produces exactly one action
scores.rationale: A concrete Phase-0 slice, dependency-ordered phases, specific technology and schema decisions, and verifiable exit checks per phase let a team start immediately and know when to change course.

checklist.evidence: Autonomous: labels, duplicate *suggestion* comments... Gated: starting resolution... Never: merge, push upstream, edit workflows.
GitHub App with least privilege: `issues:write`, `pull_requests:write`, `contents:read` on target repos, `contents:write` only on the bot fork.
All are placed in delimited data blocks and never in system instructions.
Firecracker microVM per job, no credentials inside, the clone done outside with only the tarball passed in.
reproduce (write a failing test) → localize → edit → run tests and lint → self-review → submit
an offline eval set of 500 historical closed issues with maintainer-applied labels
Outcome capture: PR merged / closed / edit distance, label corrections, review comments.
A **global kill switch** (`AGENT_WRITES_ENABLED` flag, checked before every GitHub write) exists from the first commit.
Append-only audit log: actor, action, inputs hash, prompt version, model ID, cost, GitHub object URL.
Code index (tree-sitter function/class chunks, hybrid ranking, plus live ripgrep for exact symbols. Re-indexed on push to the default branch.
A unique constraint on `delivery_id` dedupes retries.

traps.evidence: The agent never merges and never pushes to the upstream repo.
no credentials inside, the clone done outside with only the tarball passed in
the issue body is untrusted public text
Cost per merged PR drops ≥ 25% with no regression in merge rate.

note: A near-exemplary, safety-first plan that avoids every trap and concretely addresses almost the entire domain checklist; the only notable gaps are explicit bot-loop/mid-work-edit coordination and quantified build/people cost.
